title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 1981 combinatorial treatment of maps ('cartes') as sets with group actions. On the previous page the central object is a finite 'triangulated map' X: a triangulated compact surface whose vertices carry types 0, 1, ∞. R(X) is its set of triangles ('régions'). Π_{03} acts on R(X) through three fixed-point-free involutions π_0, π_1, π_∞, where π_i flips a triangle across its side opposite the vertex of type i. The 'C' version Π_{03}^C is the free product of three copies of Z/2; Π_{03} is its index-2 orientation-preserving subgroup. Π_{03} is free on ρ_0, ρ_1, ρ_∞ = products π_jπ_k, subject to ρ_0ρ_1ρ_∞ = 1. Formula (17), on the previous page, gives an equivalence between finite isotopy classes of triangulated maps and finite 'special' Π_{03}^C-sets.

This page.
(18) Orienting the surface amounts to choosing R^+(X) ⊂ R(X), a set of triangles that meets every π_i-orbit in one element. This gives an equivalence {finite oriented weighted ('pondérées') triangulated maps} ≃ {finite Π_{03}-sets}, via X ↦ R^+(X). The weights are the residual orders, so no conditions are imposed.

Duality of ordinary maps is replaced by the action of S_3 = Sym{0,1,∞}, which relabels the vertex types. Relabelling by g sends the positive triangles to the negative ones exactly when g is odd: R^+(X^g) = R^{ε(g)}(X), with ε the sign of g. In modern terms this is the action of the outer automorphisms of the free group of rank 2 (the triangle group (∞,∞,∞)) that permute the three generators, i.e. the 'hypermap operations' on dessins.

Part ③. Using the isomorphisms (15), Γ_{32} ≃ Π_{03}^C/⟨ρ_1^2⟩ and Γ_{32}^+ ≃ Π_{03}/⟨ρ_1^2⟩. Here Γ_{32} is the cartographic group of ordinary maps, presented as ⟨σ_0, σ_1, σ_2 | σ_i^2, (σ_0σ_2)^2⟩, and Γ_{32}^+ is its oriented version. It follows that the category of finite maps (folded edges allowed) is a full subcategory of the category of weighted triangulated maps, namely those with ρ_1^2 acting trivially. This is the barycentric-subdivision embedding, and similarly in the oriented case.

(19)-(20) Finally Π_{03} ≃ π_1(U_{0,3}, P_+), with U_{0,3} = P^1(C) minus {0,1,∞} and base point P_+ in the upper half-plane, conveniently taken as '−ζ', ζ = exp(2πi/3). The next page uses this to identify triangulated maps with covers of P^1 ramified only over 0, 1, ∞, i.e. dessins d'enfants via Riemann existence.

Problem served. Setting up the dictionary maps ↔ finite permutation representations of the free group ↔ covers of the thrice-punctured line ↔ curves over Q̄. This is the groundwork for the Galois action on dessins.
errors: The base point is wrong as written. −ζ = −exp(2πi/3) = exp(−iπ/3) = 1/2 − i√3/2 lies in the LOWER half-plane, not the 'hémisphère supérieur'. The intended point is presumably −ζ̄ = 1 + ζ = exp(iπ/3). That point is in the upper half-plane and is the S_3-fixed point of the anharmonic group, which explains the 'commode' choice. Alternatively this is a sign/orientation slip.
Minor: the equation number (18) is used twice, for the equivalence and for the formula R^+(X^g) = R^{ε(g)}(X).

ideas.what: Equivalence between oriented weighted triangulated (3-coloured-vertex) maps and finite Π_{03}-sets (actions of the free group F_2 = Π_{03})
ideas.modern_name: Oriented hypermaps / dessins d'enfants as finite permutation representations of the triangle group (∞,∞,∞)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cori (1975), Walsh (1975), Jones–Singerman (1978); Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984) for dessins

ideas.what: S_3 relabelling of vertex types replacing map duality, with R^+(X^g) = R^{ε(g)}(X)
ideas.modern_name: Hypermap operations (outer automorphisms of the (∞,∞,∞) triangle group / S_3 action on dessins)

ideas.what: Γ_{32}, Γ_{32}^+ as quotients of Π_{03}^C, Π_{03} by ρ_1^2; maps embedded as a full subcategory of triangulated maps
ideas.modern_name: Maps as hypermaps with one generator of order 2 (barycentric subdivision / Walsh correspondence)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (C_2 = ⟨σ_0,σ_1,σ_2 | σ_i^2, (σ_0σ_2)^2⟩, oriented C_2^+)

ideas.what: Π_{03} ≅ π_1(P^1 minus {0,1,∞}) with a symmetric base point at a sixth root of unity
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental group of the thrice-punctured sphere; S_3-symmetric tangential/ordinary base point

deep.surprise_reason: This is standard foundational material: the dictionary between hypermaps, permutation representations, covers and dessins, plus the S_3 hypermap operations. It is all present in Esquisse or in the hypermap literature of Cori, Walsh, Jones–Singerman and Machì. The only notable detail is a small slip in the choice of base point.
transcription_corrections: 'Γ_{32} ≃ \hat{Π}_{03}/⟨ρ_1^2⟩' should be Π_{03}^{C}/⟨ρ_1^2⟩, with a 'C' superscript as in (17) on the previous page, not a hat.
In (19) the base point is written P_+^* or P_+ (with a small decoration), consistent with P_+ below.
'qui n'existe pas sans dédoublement' is uncertain; the sense is that the S_3 action is essentially trivial to define.
The margin note reads roughly 'NB ici l'on vient d'identifier ... Π_{03} ... de l'action ...'; it is largely illegible and the transcription should be flagged as conjectural.
